exact_atom.question: Can Appendix D's fixed-physical-time transfer family be used as a same-theory replacement for the variable-lattice-time gap step-scaling in Theorem 5.4 without silently changing Hamiltonians, Hilbert spaces, RG maps, or continuum spectral coordinates?
success_contract: bind both transfer families to the same finite-cutoff Hamiltonian H_{k,L} on explicitly identified gauge-invariant OS Hilbert spaces
prove the exact semigroup/time-normalization relation between one-step transfer and fixed-tau transfer, including non-integer tau/a_k if used
prove compatibility of the RG embedding/intertwining with that relation and convert defects without loss that destroys a-uniformity
retain a positive defect budget after composition with issue #73

exact_atom.failure_contract: If any interface is absent from the bounded source chain, record a scoped gluing/interface obstruction only; do not infer that Appendix D's local operator lemma is false and do not make a literature-wide nonexistence claim.

source_bound_observations: Theorem 5.4 defines Delta_k=-(1/a_k) log ||T_k|Q_k|| for a one-step transfer T_k and uses a_{k+1}=b a_k.
Its exact inequality (5.36) contains exp(a_{k+1} Delta_k)||E_k||/a_{k+1}; the later bound exp(a_{k+1}Delta_k)<=exp(a_{k+1}) does not follow from Delta_k>=0 alone.
Appendix D instead fixes physical tau>0 and defines T_{k,L}=exp(-tau H_{k,L}), transfer gap 1-||T_{k,L}|Q||, and mass gap -tau^{-1} log(1-Delta_{k,L}).
Appendix D posits a scale-to-scale isometry Pi_{k,L} and defect E_{k,L}=T_{k+1,L}-Pi T_{k,L} Pi*, with summable norms uniform in L.
In the bounded locations inspected, no explicit theorem identifies the Appendix-D fixed-tau T_{k,L} with the main-text one-step transfer by a common H_{k,L} and exact semigroup/power relation.
operator_theoretic_coordinates: If S_k(t)=exp(-t H_k) is already a common strongly continuous semigroup, then ||S_k(t)|Q||=exp(-t m_k) and m_k=-t^{-1}log ||S_k(t)|Q||.
If tau=n_k a_k with integer n_k and T_k=exp(-a_k H_k), then exp(-tau H_k)=T_k^{n_k}; without a common generator this is not licensed.

For contractions A,B, ||A^n-B^n|| <= n||A-B|| by telescoping; therefore converting one-step defects to fixed physical tau can amplify errors like tau/a_k unless sharper semigroup/intertwining control is proved.

analogues.method: spectral mapping for a fixed self-adjoint Hamiltonian
analogues.transfer_assumption: same H and same excited-space projection
common generator semantics and convergence hypotheses
operators on identified spaces or exact intertwining

disanalogies: A one-lattice-step transfer family whose time increment changes with k is not automatically the same object as a fixed-physical-time semigroup family.
Vacuum-preserving isometries between scale Hilbert spaces do not by themselves identify Hamiltonian generators or logarithms.
An abstract positive-contraction interlacing lemma can be mathematically valid even when its gluing to the root theory is unproved.
Uniformity in spatial volume L does not imply uniformity in lattice spacing a_k or RG depth k.
Decay of selected Euclidean sources does not by itself imply the full physical gap; prior source-completeness obligations remain separate.
cheap_falsifiers: Set Delta_k>1: Delta_k>=0 does not imply exp(a Delta_k)<=exp(a).
Set a_k=b^k a_0 with b>1: the sequence is not uniformly comparable to 1 for all k.
Choose positive contractions with identical numerical gaps on unrelated Hilbert spaces: matching gap numbers do not establish same-theory identity.
Use ||A^n-B^n||<=n||A-B|| with n=tau/a: an O(a^0) or merely summable one-step defect need not remain a-uniform at fixed physical time.
Allow a hidden low-energy state orthogonal to controlled sources: clustering of a restricted source family still fails to certify the full Hamiltonian gap.
